title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
This incident centers on the alleged use of copyrighted sound recordings to train an AI music generation system without authorization or compensation to rights holders. The core failure is one of training-data sourcing: the system was built using material that rights holders assert they never licensed for that purpose. The problem arose before any user interaction, at the data-collection and model-training stage of development, making it invisible to any output-level review or content filter.

What this shows is a deployment pattern in which an AI system reached the public before the question of whether its training material was lawfully obtained had been resolved. Licensing agreements, if pursued at all, came after the system was already in operation, not before. The subsequent settlement and planned shift to a licensed-only platform suggest the original approach was not sustainable, though the settlements resolve commercial disputes rather than establish legal findings about the underlying copyright claims.

What is not established is whether Udio's training practices actually violated copyright law, as lawsuits are allegations and no court has issued a final ruling on the merits of these claims.

summary:
Universal Music Group has resolved its lawsuit against AI music startup Udio by reaching licensing agreements with the company. UMG had sued Udio for allegedly using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence model, claiming that hits like The Temptations' "My Girl" were used without permission or compensation. Under the settlement, Udio will launch a new platform next year that uses only authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, and share original songs through AI technology.

The agreement marks Udio's first licensing deal with a major music label and represents a shift in how the AI music industry will operate. Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees, will compensate artists who opt into the new platform, though specific details were not disclosed. UMG's CEO stated the settlement demonstrates the company's commitment to supporting artists while embracing new technologies. Additionally, UMG announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.
